summary: Digital is [pillar three of the national development programme](2025-11-19 Transform Africa Summit 2025 (Conakry) - Simandou 2040 Pillar 3, TELEMO, SANIA-SADX and the closing wrap), launched in November 2025 against a target of 20 per cent of gross domestic product.
developments:
The pillar was launched at a continental summit the country hosted, digital having previously been named one of five pillars without a target of its own ([pillar launch](2025-11-19 Transform Africa Summit 2025 (Conakry) - Simandou 2040 Pillar 3, TELEMO, SANIA-SADX and the closing wrap)).

No implementation plan, budget line or interim milestone for the target is held, so the base records an ambition stated at a summit and nothing measuring progress toward it.

summary: The digital portfolio [lost its substantive minister](2026-08-21-africa-guinee-limogeage-de-mory-conde-et-mourana) by decree in August 2026, six months after the ministry was merged and reshaped.
developments:
The ministry was formed by merger in February 2026 and the minister held it unchanged through the July 2026 reshuffle ([formation](2026-02-06-mediaguinee-mourana-soumah-takes-office-mceni), [reshuffle](2026-07-27-guinee-remaniement-gouvernement-doumbouya-juillet-2026)).

He was dismissed by presidential decree made public on 21 August 2026 with no reason given, the ministry's secretary-general appointed interim head; named successors in circulation are publications' own speculation ([dismissal](2026-08-21-africa-guinee-limogeage-de-mory-conde-et-mourana), [succession talk](2026-08-22-digital-business-guinee-mamady-doumbouya-pour-succeder-au)).

A National Assembly committee on communication and information technology was constituted and held its first working session on 7 August 2026, naming mobile money, social-media regulation and network security as priorities on its chair's own statement, with no work programme or timetable published ([committee](2026-08-07-guinea-assemblee-nationale-commission-communication-ntic)).

summary: Fibre-to-the-home is [restricted and shared-Wi-Fi activity barred](2026-05-21-mediaguinee-fesatel-ftth-wifi-zones-starlink), contested by the operators' union with a strike threat.
developments:
The union threatened to strike on 21 May 2026 over the restriction and the shared-Wi-Fi regime ([dispute](2026-05-21-mediaguinee-fesatel-ftth-wifi-zones-starlink)).

The regulator had confiscated unlicensed equipment from resellers following a communique of 30 March 2026, which predates the dispute on the record ([enforcement](2026-08-10-conversation-starlinkisation-afrique)).

No broadband plan, coverage target or licensing decision resolving either question is held, so access policy reaches the base as a licensing dispute rather than as a strategy.

summary: [Sovereign management of the country-code domain](2025-09-05 Guinea Launches National Domain .gn and Unveils First Tier III Data Center) was reinstated in September 2025, alongside the first national data centre.
developments:
The domain passed back under national management in September 2025 ([sovereign management](2025-09-05 Guinea Launches National Domain .gn and Unveils First Tier III Data Center)).

No cloud policy, hosting rule or data-localisation instrument accompanies it, so sovereignty over infrastructure is asserted through a naming registry and a building rather than through a policy.

summary: A [national AI roadmap for 2026-2035 was validated on 20 December 2025](2025-12-22-guinee-feuille-de-route-nationale-ia-2026-2035), in three phases.
developments:
[The ICT ministry announced on 20 December 2025 the validation of a national AI roadmap for 2026-2035, following a workshop with UNDP and built on an AI Landscape Assessment diagnostic the ministry says makes Guinea the first francophone country to adopt the AILA methodology](2025-12-22-guinee-feuille-de-route-nationale-ia-2026-2035). It runs in three phases: institutional, regulatory and technical foundations covering data, skills and infrastructure; progressive integration of AI into public services; then regional positioning on responsible use.

The roadmap's own text was not reachable, so its legal status, wording and indicators cannot be read off the instrument, and the announcement itself was made on the ministry's Facebook page.

summary: A [national data governance strategy went into drafting on 19 June 2026](2026-06-19-guinee-strategie-nationale-gouvernance-donnees), with no adoption date stated.
developments:
[The minister opened a stakeholder-engagement workshop on 19 June 2026 to draft a Strategie Nationale de Gouvernance des Donnees, led by the DNTIEN and covering data quality, security, interoperability and responsible use, framed within Vision Simandou 2040](2026-06-19-guinee-strategie-nationale-gouvernance-donnees).

This is the opening of a drafting process rather than an adopted framework, and the ministry states no adoption date.

summary: The [2016 cybersecurity and data-protection statute](2016-01-01-guinea-loi-l2016-037-an-cybersecurite-protection-donnees) covers processing by individuals, firms and public institutions, and is held only as an image scan.
developments:
The agency publishes it as a 57-page image-only scan with no text layer, so its provisions are the agency's summary rather than the statute's own words, and no promulgation date is published ([the statute](2016-01-01-guinea-loi-l2016-037-an-cybersecurite-protection-donnees)).

It reached the base through a summit profile rather than through the gazette ([profile](2025-11-19 Transform Africa Summit 2025 (Conakry) - Simandou 2040 Pillar 3, TELEMO, SANIA-SADX and the closing wrap)).

No implementing decree, supervisory authority, registration duty or enforcement action under its data-protection half is held.

summary: The [first conviction](2026-08-19-mediaguinee-tpi-dixinn-bella-bah-condamnation-suppression-compte-facebook) under the 2016 statute came in August 2026, and it ordered the deletion of the defendant's social-media account.
developments:
A court of first instance convicted an activist and entrepreneur of insult and defamation by means of a computer system on 19 August 2026, sentencing him to six months of which five were suspended and a 40 million GNF fine, and ordering the deletion of his account; the conviction rests on article 363 of the penal code and article 29 of the cybersecurity law ([conviction](2026-08-19-mediaguinee-tpi-dixinn-bella-bah-condamnation-suppression-compte-facebook)).

The prosecution had sought a year and argued a conviction would set an example to other social-media users; the defence, which asked for acquittal, said it would consider an appeal. Deletion of an account as a criminal penalty is something the base holds no other instance of.

The statute's cybercrime half reaches offences on national territory and those requiring collection of electronic evidence, again on the agency's summary rather than the text ([the statute](2016-01-01-guinea-loi-l2016-037-an-cybersecurite-protection-donnees), [in application](2026-07-27-guinee-ami-consultant-cybersecurite-registre-electronique-garanties)).

summary: There is [no payments statute](2026-07-31-guinee-bcrg-projets-reformes-dsmp), and the national payment council that would sit under one is at terms-of-reference stage.
developments:
Both the payments law and the council are at terms-of-reference stage under the donor programme, the law awaiting the lender's no-objection; the position comes from the central bank's own project register, which is undated and whose latest dated entry is January 2025 ([project register](2026-07-31-guinee-bcrg-projets-reformes-dsmp)).

On virtual assets the central bank issued a warning rather than a regime: it states it has granted no licence or authorisation to any entity for crypto-asset trading or online financial placement, sets out seven warning signs of fraudulent offers, notes that registration with a foreign authority is not a domestic licence, and reserves the right to refer illegal fund collection, money laundering and fraud to the courts ([communique](2026-08-20-africa-guinee-crypto-actifs-et-placements-financiers-en)).

summary: An [electronic signature decree](2026-08-19-guinee360-guinee-mamadi-doumbouya-officialise-la-signature) signed in August 2026 completes a frame that has rested since 2016 on a statute the base can only read in summary.
developments:
The 2016 statute frames electronic signature, digital archiving, certification of information systems, consumer information duties in online commerce and the related fraud and forgery offences; the agency publishes it as a 14-page image-only scan with no text layer, so the provisions are its summary rather than the statute's words ([the statute](2016-07-26-guinea-loi-l2016-035-an-transactions-electroniques)).

The 2021 implementing decree gives the telecommunications regulator supervision of electronic transactions including mobile money, with security oversight, data collection, administrative police powers and the power to levy charges on payment traffic; providers must hold a domestic or generic domain, a dedicated site and a secured transaction facility, and price in local currency inclusive of taxes and delivery ([decree](2021-03-25-guinea-decret-d-2021-092-prg-sgg-transactions-electroniques)).

The August 2026 decree gives an electronic signature the same probative force as a paper writing where it is authentic, unfalsifiable, non-reusable, unalterable and irrevocable, extends it to administrative, private-sector and person-to-person acts, and imposes duties on certification services; no certification authority is yet accredited on the record ([signature decree](2026-08-19-guinee360-guinee-mamadi-doumbouya-officialise-la-signature)).

summary: The [online legal gazette](2025-06-27-mediaguinee-journal-officiel-numerique) is free and carries more than 1,100 journals and 6,000 texts, and its index stops in April 2025.
developments:
The gazette has been online and free to access since at least June 2025 ([gazette](2025-06-27-mediaguinee-journal-officiel-numerique)).

An acquisition attempt in August 2026 found the index carrying issues only to April 2025, so a publication channel that exists has stopped being current, and no access-to-information statute, request procedure or appeal route is held beside it.

summary: The regulator [chairs the African council of regulators](2025-11-17-natca-guinea-free-roaming), and the continental summit it hosted in November 2025 has closed.
developments:
Its director-general presided at the council's fifteenth meeting alongside the summit ([chairmanship](2025-11-17-natca-guinea-free-roaming)).

The summit ran at Conakry from 12 to 19 November 2025 with 42 states and 14 memoranda, and is recorded closed ([summit](2025-11-13 Transform Africa Summit 2025 opens in Conakry, epicentre of digital cooperation in Africa)).

None of the fourteen memoranda is separately held, so what survives the summit in the base is the hosting and not its output.

progress: Advanced, the country took the presidency of the regional audiovisual regulators platform on an agenda of harmonising platform regulation
summary: The [continental cyber and data convention was ratified](2017-07-26-guinea-decret-d-2017-184-prg-sgg-ratification-convention-malabo) by decree in July 2017, and the country [took the presidency of the regional audiovisual regulators platform in August 2026](2026-08-31-africaguinee-pra-uemoa-assembly).
developments:
The ratification decree's own gazette publication is held, alongside the promulgation decree for the authorising law, the law itself remaining unheld and cited only by its long title ([ratification](2017-07-26-guinea-decret-d-2017-184-prg-sgg-ratification-convention-malabo), [promulgation](2017-07-26-guinea-decret-d-2017-178-prg-sgg-promulgation-loi-l-2017-023-an)).

The African Union's own status list records ratification or accession in July 2018 and deposit in October 2018, and the two sets of dates measure different acts. No domesticating instrument or alignment review has followed in the nine years since.

2026-08-31 — the [12th General Assembly of the audiovisual regulators platform of the eight monetary-union states and Guinea opened in Conakry, and its presidency passed to Guinea](2026-08-31-africaguinee-pra-uemoa-assembly), the head of the national communications authority taking its leadership. The two-day agenda was harmonising the legal and technical tools for regulating social platforms against cybersecurity and social-cohesion risks, including AI-generated disinformation and deepfakes, and strengthening the standing of regulators over digital platforms. The Justice Minister opened it arguing for a framework that [protects without stifling and regulates without censoring, and calling cybersecurity a question of sovereignty rather than a technical one](2026-08-31-africaguinee-garde-des-sceaux-cyberespace). No harmonised instrument, timetable or funding is announced, so what the base holds is a presidency and an agenda.

summary: A [free-roaming protocol with Sierra Leone](2025-11-17-natca-guinea-free-roaming) was signed in November 2025, on a border interconnection raised to 100 Gbps.
developments:
The protocol was signed at the regulators' council meeting; no implementation date or tariff is on file ([protocol](2025-11-17-natca-guinea-free-roaming)).

The backbone interconnection between the two countries was raised from 42.5 Gbps to 100 Gbps under a 2024 bilateral pact ([interconnection](2025-06-23-sogeb-leonecom-fibre-interconnection)).

The capacity is the base's only measured piece of regional infrastructure, and no traffic figure across it is published.

summary: An [open government-stack standards workshop](2026-04-08-techreviewafrica-govstack-workshop-wardip) was held under the donor programme, with no standard adopted on the record.
developments:
The workshop is the whole of the record on standards adoption ([workshop](2026-04-08-techreviewafrica-govstack-workshop-wardip)).

No conformance profile, building-block selection or compliance requirement has followed it, though the two interoperability platforms later presented to the prime minister are built in that programme's frame.

summary: Facebook, YouTube and TikTok have been [restricted since 28 July 2026](2026-07-28-guinee-ablogui-blocage-cible-facebook-youtube-tiktok) with no authority acknowledging it and no official explanation held.
developments:
The blocking was measured from 28 July and was still running on 7 August 2026, while the President was abroad ([measurement](2026-07-28-guinee-ablogui-blocage-cible-facebook-youtube-tiktok), [still running](2026-08-07-guinee-des-reseaux-sociaux-coupes-alors-que-mamadi-doumbouya-est-a-letranger)).

A consumer union additionally reports one messaging service restricted and bandwidth broadly reduced for several months, with internet providers and mobile operators stating the decision was not theirs ([union account](2026-08-04-guinee-bany-sidibe-denonce-restrictions-reseaux-sociaux-degradation-internet)), and businesses report disruption ([disruption](2026-07-30-guinea-social-media-restrictions-disrupt-businesses)).

A total two-hour national outage on 7 August 2026 was traced to the state landing-station operator, whose officials and the regulator both declined to explain it ([outage](2026-08-12-guinea-internet-blackout-guilab-accountability)).

summary: A [3 per cent compliance fee on foreign digital services](2026-05-26-ecofin-guinea-3pct-tax-foreign-digital-services) was decreed in May 2026 to finance a new digital sovereignty fund.
developments:
The fee runs at a flat 3 per cent for twelve months and then 1.5 to 7 per cent by service category, with an exemption below 250m GNF of annual taxable revenue, given in the source as roughly US$28,600 ([decree](2026-05-26-ecofin-guinea-3pct-tax-foreign-digital-services)); a six-month transition precedes enforcement ([decree](2026-05-26-ecofin-guinea-3pct-tax-foreign-digital-services)).

The same decree creates a digital sovereignty fund financed primarily from the fee, with no capitalisation, governance or first disbursement published, and a digital analysis and regulation platform to monitor foreign digital services, which is not on record as operating.

No domestic budget appropriation for digital transformation is held at any date, so a hypothecated levy on foreign providers is the only financing instrument the base can see.

summary: An [international card network opened talks](2026-04-12-techreviewafrica-visa-engages-guinea-digital-payments) with the finance ministry in April 2026 toward a central-bank memorandum.
developments:
Nothing is signed on the record ([talks](2026-04-12-techreviewafrica-visa-engages-guinea-digital-payments)).

It is the only strategic commercial relationship in the base that is not a construction contract or a donor credit, and no scope, value or timetable is published for it.

progress: No change, an aggregate the wiki compiled rather than a published figure
summary: Tracked non-state finance stands at [US$543m across five deals](2024-01-01-miga-gin-orange-guinea-2024-orange-guinea-telecoms-operator-guarantee-sonatel) for 2023 to 2025, compiled rather than published.
developments:
The aggregate is drawn from the deal records held rather than from any published statement, and carries no source of its own ([aggregate](2024-01-01-miga-gin-orange-guinea-2024-orange-guinea-telecoms-operator-guarantee-sonatel)).

No investment promotion figure, private capital commitment or sector-level series exists against which to read it, so the number is a floor on what has been found rather than a measure of what has been raised.

summary: The [US$60m regional digital credit](2026-07-27-guinee-ami-it-wardip-3-termes-de-reference) is under implementation, with a rescue consultancy tendered for its collateral registry in July 2026.
developments:
The programme carries the payments law and the payment council at terms-of-reference stage, and tendered a rescue consultancy for the movable-collateral registry on 27 July 2026 ([programme](2026-07-27-guinee-ami-it-wardip-3-termes-de-reference)).

It is the single donor operation the base holds for the sector, and it is also the vehicle for the interoperability platforms, the standards workshop and the registry, so a delay in it stops several workstreams at once.

summary: The state [holds 87.5 per cent of the second mobile operator](2025-01-06-connectingafrica-mtn-sells-guinea-conakry-to-state), transferred at the end of 2024, on about 3m subscribers.
developments:
The transfer was made official on 30 December 2024 ([transfer](2025-01-06-connectingafrica-mtn-sells-guinea-conakry-to-state)).

No regulator subscription series, penetration rate or market-share figure is published at any date, so a single operator's subscriber count carried in a transfer report is the whole of the connectivity measurement the base holds.

progress: Advanced, on the ministry's own figure
summary: Mobile internet cost was [reported down 25 per cent over 2025](2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026) in the ministry's sector review, with no baseline price published.
developments:
The reduction is ministry-reported and carries no starting price, tariff basket or basis of comparison ([sector review](2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026)).

No regulator tariff series, affordability index or income-share measure exists against which to read it, so the direction is stated and the level is not.

summary: The backbone's first loop [went from 200 to 400 Gb/s on 20 May 2026, with 600 Gb/s targeted by year end](2026-05-22-guinee-backbone-capacite-400-gbs-huawei).
developments:
[SOGEB announced on 20 May 2026 that the first loop of the national fibre backbone had been raised from 200 Gb/s to 400 Gb/s with Huawei's technical support, the second upgrade in eighteen months after December 2024's step from 50 Gb/s to 200 Gb/s — a cumulative 700% increase — with both partners targeting 600 Gb/s across the whole infrastructure by the end of the year](2026-05-22-guinee-backbone-capacite-400-gbs-huawei).

The same account carries the regulator's traffic series, mobile internet traffic rising from 23.98 million GB in the second quarter of 2021 to 118.86 million GB in the second quarter of 2025. No utilisation figure against the upgraded capacity is held.

summary: The [single 2012 landing is saturated](2025-07-10-mediaguinee-second-submarine-cable-workshop), and agreements are now signed or agreed for a second and a third cable.
developments:
The cable has been the country's only landing for about thirteen to fifteen years and is named saturated ([sole landing](2025-07-10-mediaguinee-second-submarine-cable-workshop)).

A construction and maintenance agreement was signed in August 2026 to land a Mediterranean-anchored system at Conakry, with the state-majority landing party alongside a mobile operator; no timeline is given for the 8,700km, 19-landing-site system ([second landing](2026-08-19-data-center-medusa-subsea-cable-land-guinea), [agreement](2026-05-06-mediaguinee-medusa-africa-second-submarine-cable-cma)).

Co-investment in a third system was agreed in Paris in June 2026 with no landing date published ([third landing](2026-06-17-mediaguinee-via-africa-third-submarine-cable)).

No capacity figure, price or utilisation is published for the existing link or the two planned, so saturation is asserted and not measured.

summary: The exchange point's executive secretary [represented the country at the fifteenth continental peering forum](2026-09-01-guinee-afpif-2026-ixp-participation), and the base holds no traffic or member figure for the exchange itself.
developments:
The national internet exchange point was represented at the fifteenth African peering and interconnection forum in Kigali from 17 to 20 August 2026, supported by the communications, digital economy and innovation ministry through a regional digital integration programme, with the stated aim of strengthening its place in the continental interconnection network ([forum](2026-09-01-guinee-afpif-2026-ixp-participation)).

Attendance is what is recorded. No peering agreement, member count, traffic figure or local-traffic share is published for the exchange point, so whether domestic traffic stays in the country is not established.

summary: One satellite provider is [stated not to be recognised](2026-05-21-mediaguinee-fesatel-ftth-wifi-zones-starlink) in the country, and no licensing decision is on file.
developments:
The operators' union made the statement in May 2026 in the course of its dispute over access licensing ([union statement](2026-05-21-mediaguinee-fesatel-ftth-wifi-zones-starlink)).

No authorisation, refusal, framework or enforcement action on satellite broadband is held at any date, so the position is a third party's characterisation rather than a regulatory decision.

summary: A [national data centre](2025-09-04 Guinea opens Tier 3 national data centre to strengthen digital transition) certified to the third tier was inaugurated at Conakry in September 2025, the first in the country.
developments:
It is in service and externally certified ([inauguration](2025-09-04 Guinea opens Tier 3 national data centre to strengthen digital transition)).

No rack count, power capacity, occupancy, tenant list or hosting policy is published for it, so the base records a building and nothing about what runs in it.

progress: Mixed, two administrative tools were launched while the central bank's core settlement migration stalled on unpaid invoices
summary: A [decrees and orders management tool](2026-08-14-guinea-geda-doumbouya-decrets-arretes) and a [mission-order system](2026-08-13-guinea-geme-digitalisation-missions-etat) went into use, while the settlement system's message migration is stalled.
developments:
The President stated on 14 August 2026 that he would personally oversee the decrees tool to speed administrative processing, tied to the national development programme; no throughput figure, custodian or publication rule is stated, and personal oversight by the head of state is not an institutional control ([decrees tool](2026-08-14-guinea-geda-doumbouya-decrets-arretes)).

The mission-order system was launched on 13 August 2026 to control costs and improve accountability, with no custodian, coverage, cost baseline or saving target stated ([mission orders](2026-08-13-guinea-geme-digitalisation-missions-etat)).

The real-time settlement system's migration to the international messaging standard has not been made, held by unpaid invoices to the supplier and prolonged customs clearance after a second equipment lot was delivered in January 2025 ([project register](2026-07-31-guinee-bcrg-projets-reformes-dsmp)).

The central bank has an international tender open for a resilient messaging infrastructure, single lot, financed from its own resources, with bids due 31 August 2026 ([tender](2026-07-30-bcrg-appel-offres-moderniser-infrastructure-swift), [notice](2026-07-01-bcrg-guinea-avis-appel-offres-infrastructure-swift)).

summary: The [national cybersecurity agency](2025-09-09 Get to know The Republic of Guinea Home of Transform Africa Summit 2025) is established, with no published mandate, budget or reporting on file.
developments:
It is named as an established agency in a summit host profile and no founding instrument for it is held ([agency](2025-09-09 Get to know The Republic of Guinea Home of Transform Africa Summit 2025)).

No incident statistics, response team, sector designation or audit programme is published, so the agency that publishes the country's cybersecurity statute as an image scan is itself known only by name.

summary: [X-Road is named as the national interoperability platform and described as in progress rather than in production](2026-08-20-guinee-etat-interconnexion-x-road-e-service).
developments:
[The Prime Minister was shown the state of the national e-service portal and of X-Road, the national interoperability platform run by ANDE, whose function is to let public information systems communicate so users need not supply the same information repeatedly; he asked that the tools improve traceability and reduce fraud, and announced the forthcoming creation of an interministerial committee on state digitalisation](2026-08-20-guinee-etat-interconnexion-x-road-e-service).

This is the first located account naming the platform. No decret, arrete or inter-agency protocol establishing it was found, and it is described as in progress, not in production.

summary: A [One Health steering committee](2026-08-14-guinea-une-seule-sante-plateforme-nationale) signed a four-ministry data-sharing protocol in August 2026, on a health system still at workshop stage.
developments:
Five health facilities in the Mamou and Dalaba districts now run a hospital information system with interoperability to the national health platform, and the Dalaba prefectural hospital reports consultations up ([report](2026-08-26-lepandaguinee-guinee-a-mamou-et-dalaba-le-pari-de)). Five facilities is the extent the base can state.

The health, higher education, environment and livestock ministries signed a protocol for shared data, joint epidemiological surveillance and coordinated response to zoonotic and environmental risk; no platform build, data-sharing rule, custodian or protection standard for the shared health and animal data is stated ([protocol](2026-08-14-guinea-une-seule-sante-plateforme-nationale)).

The health information system's own interoperability work is a Conakry workshop and a maternity register piloted in 15 centres ([workshop](2025-11-27 Interoperability - key workshop to modernize Guinea's health information system)).

summary: A [unique personal identification number](2026-08-11-guinee-decentralisation-etat-civil-npi) is stated to be being put in place, with no instrument, issuing authority or format on record.
developments:
The statement was made by the territorial administration minister at a commemorative event in August 2026, alongside digitalisation of the civil-status system, and is not an instrument ([statement](2026-08-11-guinee-decentralisation-etat-civil-npi)).

The unified social register has meanwhile operated since 2019 without a unique identifier, which is the concrete cost of the number's absence ([social register](2025-11-30 Guinea Claims $26.9M Saved Since 2024 with Biometric Audit of Public Workforce (FUGAS))).

summary: Biometric enrolment [opened in one commune](2026-03-04 Guinea Launches Biometric Birth Certificates in Sanoyah in Civil Registry Modernization Push) in March 2026 on a first phase of 2,000 certificates, after the predecessor project closed with about 8,000 identities.
developments:
The earlier foundational project closed on 28 June 2024, two years early, having issued about 8,000 unique identities ([closure](2025-05-02 WURI Implementation Status Report - Cote d'Ivoire and Guinea (P161329 Seq 11))).

Enrolment for biometric birth certificates and national identity opened in Sanoyah commune as phase one ([enrolment](2026-03-04 Guinea Launches Biometric Birth Certificates in Sanoyah in Civil Registry Modernization Push)).

Issuance was decreed free in February 2025, and the state contractor alleged in July 2026 that unprovided-for fees and pay-for-priority were being taken at enrolment centres, with no ministerial response on file ([fees alleged](2026-07-28-guinee-mgg-denonce-racket-etat-civil-biometrique)).

progress: Mixed, the registration rate rose while the paper the certificate is printed on ran out
summary: Birth registration was [put at 72 per cent for 2025](2026-08-11-guinee-decentralisation-etat-civil-npi) from 54 per cent in 2022, on a base where communes ran out of secured paper.
developments:
The figures are the territorial administration minister's own, given in a ceremonial statement with no statistical source named ([minister's figures](2026-08-11-guinee-decentralisation-etat-civil-npi)).

A civil-registration officer said on 7 August 2026 that the secured paper the digital birth certificate is printed on had run out, leaving communes across the capital and beyond unable to issue extracts for about a month; his own commune processes all applicants regardless of home commune and holds reserve stock for urgent cases ([stockout](2026-08-07-guinea-secure-paper-shortage-birth-certificates)).

No ministry statement, restocking date or national count of affected communes is held.

summary: A [biometric civil-service payroll audit](2025-11-30 Guinea Claims $26.9M Saved Since 2024 with Biometric Audit of Public Workforce (FUGAS)) confirmed about 130,000 of about 277,000 registered staff and reports 233bn GNF saved since 2024.
developments:
The system has been in use since 2024 with no audit result published before this one ([audit](2025-11-30 Guinea Claims $26.9M Saved Since 2024 with Biometric Audit of Public Workforce (FUGAS))).

The saving is about US$26.9m at the reported date and is the government's own claim ([audit](2025-11-30 Guinea Claims $26.9M Saved Since 2024 with Biometric Audit of Public Workforce (FUGAS))); no methodology, payroll series or independent verification is held, and the audit confirmed under half of those registered.

summary: [NimbaPay launched on 22 July 2026 as the national instant and interoperable payment platform](2026-07-22-bcrg-guim-lancement-nimbapay-paiement-instantane).
developments:
[NimbaPay was officially launched on 22 July 2026 under the Prime Minister's patronage, operated by the Guineenne de la Monetique under the central bank, letting any user send and receive money instantly between a bank, a microfinance institution and an electronic-money establishment](2026-07-22-bcrg-guim-lancement-nimbapay-paiement-instantane). [The governor said fragmented systems had been penalising inter-institutional transfers, and named digitisation of state payments and cross-border flows as the next steps](2026-07-22-bcrg-guim-lancement-nimbapay-paiement-instantane).

No transaction volume or participant count is held for the platform since launch.

summary: A [public-payments gateway](2025-12-23 Guinea rolls out Tresor Pay as digital gateway for public payments) launched in December 2025 for state administrative fees by mobile, alongside social contributions at about 60 per cent online.
developments:
The gateway entered service on 22 December 2025 ([gateway](2025-12-23 Guinea rolls out Tresor Pay as digital gateway for public payments)).

The social-security platform carries about 60 per cent of contribution receipts ([contributions](2025-07-09-mediaguinee-cnss-ecnss-platform)).

No collection volume, value or fee arrangement is published for either, so the share of state revenue collected digitally is unmeasured.

summary: A [national instant payment system](2026-07-28-guinea-ecofin-nimbapay-national-instant-payment-system) opened in July 2026, interoperable across banks, electronic-money institutions and microfinance.
developments:
It was built in 127 days on an open-source core by the national card company with a continental payments foundation and a technical partner, and went live nationwide on 22 July 2026 ([launch](2026-07-28-guinea-ecofin-nimbapay-national-instant-payment-system), [opening](2026-07-22-mediaguinee-nimbapay-lancement)).

The separate national switch project, memorandum signed in December 2024, is not operational as a switch in its own right ([project register](2026-07-31-guinee-bcrg-projets-reformes-dsmp)).

No transaction volume, value or participant count has been published in the month since the system opened.

summary: [Account access rose from 4% of adults in 2011 to close to 36% in 2024 on the central bank governor's account](2026-07-22-bcrg-guim-lancement-nimbapay-paiement-instantane).
developments:
[At the NimbaPay launch on 22 July 2026 the central bank governor put access to financial accounts at 4% in 2011 and close to 36% in 2024, attributing the rise to electronic money](2026-07-22-bcrg-guim-lancement-nimbapay-paiement-instantane).

The figure is the governor's own, given in a launch speech; the base holds no survey series behind it and no breakdown by sex, region or income.

summary: The country is a [participant in the pan-African settlement system with no transaction recorded](2026-07-31-guinee-bcrg-projets-reformes-dsmp), and the regional payment project was withdrawn.
developments:
Participant status carries no recorded transaction on the platform ([project register](2026-07-31-guinee-bcrg-projets-reformes-dsmp)).

The regional integrated payment project was withdrawn from the central bank's 2025 strategic priorities after a single evaluation meeting in July 2024, with no visibility on next steps.

Both readings come from the same undated register, so the country's cross-border position is established entirely by one internal document.

summary: A consumer union [published twelve conditions](2026-07-26-guinee-aguiduten-salue-lancement-nimbapay) on the new instant payment system the day after launch, and they are unanswered.
developments:
Neither the regulator nor the operator has responded on the record ([conditions](2026-07-26-guinee-aguiduten-salue-lancement-nimbapay)).

No complaints procedure, redress mechanism, tariff transparency rule or dispute statistic exists for digital payments anywhere in the base, so an unanswered civil-society list is the whole of the consumer-protection record.

summary: An [administrative census delivered secured civil-registry inputs](2026-03-03-mediaguinee-pn-ravec-secured-civil-registry-intrants-rgph4) to the population register, which is now the single official source for the electoral roll.
developments:
Enumeration ran from 15 April 2025 and its outputs feed the population register and the census ([census](2026-03-03-mediaguinee-pn-ravec-secured-civil-registry-intrants-rgph4)).

A convention between the elections directorate and the civil-registry office institutionalised data sharing from the register to the roll, making it the roll's single official source ([convention](2026-01-22-mediaguinee-dge-oneci-convention-fichier-electoral)).

No registration completeness figure, record count or update rule for the register itself is published.

summary: The [movable-collateral electronic registry](2026-07-27-guinee-ami-it-wardip-3-termes-de-reference) has software built and none of the institutional, legal or regulatory provisions it needs.
developments:
A rescue consultancy was tendered under the donor programme in July 2026, opening on the 27th and closing on 17 August ([rescue tender](2026-07-27-guinee-ami-it-wardip-3-termes-de-reference)).

Its security posture and user base are also not in place, so a system that exists as code has no legal effect, which is the clearest instance in this ledger of a build running ahead of its statute.

summary: The [unified social register](2025-01-01 Registre Social Unifie (RSU) presentation - Guinea) has operated since a 2019 decree without a unique identifier.
developments:
It was created by decree in October 2019 and its position is unchanged ([register](2025-01-01 Registre Social Unifie (RSU) presentation - Guinea)).

No beneficiary count, coverage figure, update cycle or link to the civil registry is published, and the absence of an identifier is what the number now being announced would have to fix.

summary: The [permanent biometric electoral file](2026-04-25-mediaguinee-fichier-electoral-7m-elections-couplees) held 6.95m electors across 23,681 stations for the May 2026 coupled elections.
developments:
It stood at 6.77m at the September 2025 referendum ([earlier file](2025-08-28-mediaguinee-definitive-biometric-electoral-file)) and at 6.95m with 23,681 stations by April 2026 ([current file](2026-04-25-mediaguinee-fichier-electoral-7m-elections-couplees)).

It is the base's most precisely stated register, and its precision comes from an election timetable rather than from a registry publication.

summary: A [first phase of the Systeme d'Information Foncier covering Conakry and thirteen towns was agreed in October 2025](2025-10-12-lancement-systeme-information-foncier-guinee).
developments:
[The urbanism minister and Geo Consult International set the terms of the first implementation phase of the Systeme d'Information Foncier, covering Conakry and thirteen other towns, on five pillars: high-resolution aerial imagery, a structured parcel plan for Conakry, a multi-actor land survey campaign, the system itself, and the supporting technical infrastructure and training; financing for a national phase was under discussion with the Islamic Development Bank](2025-10-12-lancement-systeme-information-foncier-guinee).

[Separately, mapping of State agricultural land began in Boke, Conakry, Kankan and Kindia on 6 October 2025 under the agricultural land reform, centralising areas and coordinates in a national database connected to a future e-Foncier rural platform](2025-10-14-cartographie-terres-agricoles-e-foncier-rural).

Both are first phases: no parcel count, coverage figure or completion date is held for either.

summary: A private platform is [deployed in 19 hospitals](2026-08-13-guinea-kouma-academy-hospital-digitisation-financing) with more than a million users, and a blood-supply platform coordinates across the region.
developments:
The hospital platform runs on a self-financed model and is being extended to Chad, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Morocco; the figures are a private academy's own, with no ministry acknowledgement, patient-data protection arrangement or interoperability with the national health information system stated ([hospital platform](2026-08-13-guinea-kouma-academy-hospital-digitisation-financing)).

A platform founded in 2022 coordinates blood donation and blood-bank logistics across West Africa from Guinea, to stop units expiring at one facility while another is short; no facility count, transfer volume, ministry relationship or health-data protection arrangement is stated ([blood platform](2026-08-17-esdras-azanmassou-ayooka-blood-donation-network)).

Both are private, and the state's own health information system is at workshop and pilot stage.

summary: An [e-procurement platform](2026-08-22-guinee360-commande-publique-en-guinee-mamadi-doumbouya) now digitises the full procurement cycle, with a decree of August 2026 fixing the rules for taking paper out of the process.
developments:
The decree of 21 August 2026, made under article 56 of the 2019 procurement code, provides for a national electronic platform for public contracts and public-private partnerships managed by the finance ministry, mandatory registration of contracting authorities and bidders, and encrypted bid submission; it does not state whether the national platform is this one or a successor ([decree](2026-08-22-guinee360-commande-publique-en-guinee-mamadi-doumbouya), [platform](2026-05-26-techafricanews-telemo-procurement-platform-launch)). A joint government mission went to Kigali in August 2026 for talks covering the platform's evolution ([mission](2026-08-18-guinee-jet-guinee-rwanda-conakry-renforce-sa-cooperation)).

An industrial-permits platform issues licences in 72 hours as successor to an earlier system ([permits](2026-01-12-mediaguinee-landaya-industrial-permits-platform)).

A single window for public services is agreed with Azerbaijan on its own service model, with no launch date published ([single window](2026-03-17-mediaguinee-guichet-unique-services-publics-azerbaijan-asan)), inside a package of nine announced projects covering human-resources systems, a government laboratory, electronic tax, an information-technology inventory, digital skills and the biometric payroll ([package](2026-05-18-wearetech-nine-digital-projects-public-administration)).

summary: [Computer and solar kits were awarded for 21 local authorities and seven rural communes on 1 October 2025](2025-10-07-anafic-attribution-kits-informatiques-solaires-collectivites).
developments:
[ANAFIC awarded two lots under AFD C2D financing on 1 October 2025: computer kits for 21 local authorities — the 14 Conakry communes plus the Gouvernorat and seven communes of the interior — at GNF 836,500,000, and solar kits for seven new rural communes of the interior at GNF 781,060,000, both procured explicitly to run the commune accounting and financial management software](2025-10-07-anafic-attribution-kits-informatiques-solaires-collectivites).

It is hardware and off-grid power rather than connectivity: no rural broadband programme, white-zones plan or rural digital-services document is held.

summary: A school connectivity plan targets [2,200 primary schools by the end of 2026](2025-11-07 Guinea Kicks Off Plan to Bring Internet to 2,200 Schools), with 585 connected by January.
developments:
The plan was launched on 5 November 2025 ([plan](2025-11-07 Guinea Kicks Off Plan to Bring Internet to 2,200 Schools)) and 585 schools were connected by January 2026 ([progress](2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026)).

No later figure is published, so a programme with a hard end-of-year target is last measured at about a quarter of it with eleven months gone.

summary: A [national programme entered its second phase](2026-04-03-techreviewafrica-douia2-ai-manifesto-conakry) with a Conakry manifesto signed in April 2026, and cooperation areas were identified with Rwanda.
developments:
The first phase closed and the second launched with the manifesto's signature; the only account on file is from a wire outlet and no primary document, workplan or budget is held ([programme](2026-04-03-techreviewafrica-douia2-ai-manifesto-conakry)).

Artificial intelligence, electronic health, electronic commerce and electronic invoicing were identified for exploration with Rwanda at a Conakry meeting in July 2026, widening a cooperation previously limited to public-finance digitisation; nothing is signed ([cooperation](2026-07-21-guinee-rwanda-explorent-nouveaux-projets-e-sante-ia)).

summary: A [Guinea-founded cross-border payments firm](2026-04-14-techcabal-cauridor-appoints-coo) operates in 36 countries, and is the only domestic technology firm the base names.
developments:
It appointed a chief operating officer in April 2026 ([appointment](2026-04-14-techcabal-cauridor-appoints-coo)).

No sector output figure, employment count, firm register or startup instrument exists anywhere in the base, so one company's country count is the entire measure of national capacity in production.

progress: Stalled, the startup law has been in draft since April 2025 with no act promulgated
summary: [The startup law was still a draft under relecture in April 2025](2025-04-29-seance-relecture-projet-loi-startups-guinee), and no act has been published.
developments:
[The commerce ministry's secretary general chaired a relecture session on the draft startup law on 29 April 2025, with the higher education and telecommunications ministries, stating its objects as an adapted legal and fiscal environment, better access to finance and public-private partnerships, and stronger competitiveness for young innovative firms](2025-04-29-seance-relecture-projet-loi-startups-guinee). No promulgated act, law number or Journal Officiel publication is held.

[A Guinean startup alliance was founded in October 2025](2025-10-29-naissance-guinee-alliance-startups), [the SabouTech incubator is running](2026-01-01-saboutech-incubateur-innovation-guinee), and [a national innovation strategy was put out to tender in August 2026](2026-08-17-enabel-marche-strategie-nationale-innovation-guinee). No innovation fund instrument is held.

summary: A [fourth FabLab Solidaire opened at Coyah on 3 June 2026, the first outside Conakry](2026-06-12-quatrieme-fablab-solidaire-coyah-fondation-orange-guinee).
developments:
[The Fondation Orange Guinee, with the Agence Francaise de Developpement, inaugurated a fourth FabLab Solidaire at the Ecole Regionale des Arts et Metiers of Coyah on 3 June 2026, the first of the four outside Conakry; the network since 2022 runs at the Orange Digital Center de Ratoma, the Ecole Nationale des Postes et Telecommunications at Kipe and the SankuLab de Bellevue, with stated targets of training more than 125 women in green trades and digital technologies and at least 30% of beneficiaries developing an income-generating activity](2026-06-12-quatrieme-fablab-solidaire-coyah-fondation-orange-guinee).

This is a programme count and not a measurement: no digital-literacy rate for the population is held at any date, and the four labs are a private foundation's, not the state's.

summary: A [distance-learning institute was erected into a digital university](2026-07-31-isfad-devient-universite-numerique-de-guinee-ung) by decree in July 2026, and a software-engineering campus opened the same month.
developments:
The decree makes it a public scientific establishment with legal personality and an 11-member governing board, its mandate covering online higher education, continuing education and digital-pedagogy support, with implementation assigned to three ministers; no programme, budget or launch date for the online offerings is published ([decree](2026-07-31-isfad-devient-universite-numerique-de-guinee-ung)).

A private software-engineering campus launched at Conakry on 16 July 2026 ([campus](2026-07-17-holberton-guinee-launch)).

progress: Advanced, on the ministry's own figure
summary: [More than 10,000 people](2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026) were reported trained in digital skills in the ministry's 2025 sector review.
developments:
The figure is ministry-reported with no cohort breakdown, course list, completion rate or destination data behind it ([sector review](2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026)).

No literacy measurement, employment outcome or baseline exists against which to read it, and the base holds no digital literacy programme or measurement of any kind.

summary: A [West African mathematics institute is teaching a pilot cohort of 45 students inside the national university](2025-12-10-mesrsi-institut-ouest-africain-mathematiques-uganc).
developments:
[The Institut Ouest-Africain de Mathematiques has been structured inside the Universite Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, with two associate lecturers recruited from Benin and Senegal and a pilot cohort of 45 Guinean and foreign students already teaching ahead of the official opening](2025-12-10-mesrsi-institut-ouest-africain-mathematiques-uganc).

No research output, funding line or programme budget is held for it, and nothing states what it contributes to digital or data policy.

summary: A [civil-service housing registration platform](2026-08-24-mediaguinee-logements-sociaux-plateforme-inscription-gouvernement) opened in August 2026, its communique warning that payments made outside it engage no government responsibility.
developments:
The ministry directed officials to use the official platform alone to complete an interest survey and to read the eligibility conditions, warning that no registration, fee or intervention made outside the announced arrangement engages the government's responsibility ([communique](2026-08-24-mediaguinee-logements-sociaux-plateforme-inscription-gouvernement)).

The warning is the notable part: it names the fraud the platform is meant to displace.

A national vehicle-attestation platform was contracted to two foreign suppliers in August 2025 with no service date published ([vehicle platform](2025-08-01-aminata-national-vehicle-attestation-platform-siin-digitech)).

summary: Guinea is one of five states whose [second submarine cable bids were evaluated](2026-07-06-ecowas-wardip-submarine-cable-capacity-evaluation-committee) at Abuja in July 2026.
developments:
The [evaluation committee meeting of 29 June to 10 July 2026](2026-07-06-ecowas-wardip-submarine-cable-capacity-evaluation-committee) covers five member states under the regional digital programme, Guinea among them, and assesses bids for capacity on a second West African submarine cable.

Domestically, the financing that reaches administrations outside the capital is the [US$81m local governance credit whose component split was confirmed in June 2025](2025-06-20-world-bank-guinea-pagl2-p177095-isr-financing-components).

summary: The [fourth population census](2026-04-25-mediaguinee-fichier-electoral-7m-elections-couplees) produced a population of 17,521,167, carried into the electoral file.
developments:
The figure reaches the base through the electoral file's own account rather than through a statistical publication ([census figure](2026-04-25-mediaguinee-fichier-electoral-7m-elections-couplees)).

No census report, survey programme or dissemination platform is held, so the country's population is established by the register that consumed it.

summary: A [public finance statistics committee](2026-08-08-guinea-comite-statistiques-finances-publiques) was relaunched in August 2026 and still faces inconsistent data across the Treasury and the central bank.
developments:
Created in 2023, it is sitting again and producing a regular statement of state financial operations against the 2014 international manual ([relaunch](2026-08-08-guinea-comite-statistiques-finances-publiques)).

The account of the remaining inconsistency is the finance ministry's own, which makes it the base's only admission that two arms of the state hold different numbers for the same transactions.

progress: No change, a standing statute the base holds for the first time
summary: [Loi L/2020/0027/AN requires proactive publication of sixteen categories of public information and makes re-use free by default](2020-12-19-loi-2020-0027-an-acces-information-publique); no portal implements it.
developments:
[The access-to-information law's Article 10 imposes proactive publication, refreshed at least quarterly, of sixteen categories including statistical, economic and social information, budget and public-finance data at central, regional and local level, national accounts, public debt and procurement projects, and Article 11 requires the site to carry the legal framework, request forms and appeal routes](2020-12-19-loi-2020-0027-an-acces-information-publique). [Chapitre 3, Articles 27 to 32, governs re-use: public information may be re-used for other purposes, restrictions only on proportionate general-interest grounds, and re-use free of charge by default with cost-recovery fees only for commercial re-use](2020-12-19-loi-2020-0027-an-acces-information-publique).

The statute is held and no national open-data portal implementing it is. Nothing states how many requests are received, how many are granted, or whether any refusal has been appealed.

summary: A [connected-farmers cohort](2026-08-07-guinea-kumy-crg-agriculteurs-connectes) launched in August 2026 pairs field sensors and weather alerts with a state rural bank's 1,000-plus service points.
developments:
The first cohort runs as a private partnership with a state-owned bank rather than as a public programme, and no cohort size, cost or coverage is stated ([cohort](2026-08-07-guinea-kumy-crg-agriculteurs-connectes)).

No earth-observation or satellite data programme exists anywhere in the base, so agronomic advice delivered through a bank's branch network is the whole of the record.

summary: A [CREWS project rebuilt the meteorological service and put 28 stations on the WMO Information System](2026-02-05-crews-project-improves-meteorological-service-guinea).
developments:
[A US$250,000 CREWS Accelerated Support Window project closed in October 2025, rebuilding the national meteorological service after the 18 December 2023 Conakry fuel-depot explosion destroyed much of its infrastructure: a website carrying WIS2box and a CAP composer, 113 warning bulletins published in CAP format for rain, storms and lightning, 28 stations revised and connected to the WMO database and Information System, and temporary premises and reliable internet for the agency](2026-02-05-crews-project-improves-meteorological-service-guinea). [Guinea is the first African country onboarded by Google Public Alert](2026-02-05-crews-project-improves-meteorological-service-guinea).

GBON compliance is stated as still to follow under a successor project, and no satellite data source is named for any other sector.

summary: United States providers of [streaming, cloud, software and advertising services were brought into charge](2026-05-26-ecofin-guinea-3pct-tax-foreign-digital-services) by the May 2026 decree.
developments:
The decree requires a local representative to be appointed within 90 days and applies to streaming, cloud, software-as-a-service, advertising and electronic commerce ([decree](2026-05-26-ecofin-guinea-3pct-tax-foreign-digital-services)).

It is the only instrument in the base that touches American technology companies, and it taxes them rather than partnering with them; no memorandum, investment or engagement with any of them is held.

summary: Huawei [raised the backbone's first loop from 200 to 400 Gb/s on 20 May 2026](2026-05-22-guinee-backbone-capacite-400-gbs-huawei) and is [in talks toward a comprehensive memorandum](2026-07-03-guinea-huawei-deepen-strategic-partnership).
developments:
[The backbone operator SOGEB announced on 20 May 2026 that the first loop of the national fibre backbone had gone from 200 Gb/s to 400 Gb/s with Huawei's technical support, the second upgrade in eighteen months after December 2024's step from 50 Gb/s, with 600 Gb/s across the whole infrastructure targeted by year end](2026-05-22-guinee-backbone-capacite-400-gbs-huawei). [Huawei designed and built the roughly 4,300 to 4,500 km backbone and remains its technical partner on capacity](2026-05-22-guinee-backbone-capacite-400-gbs-huawei).

[Talks in China on 3 July 2026 between the communication and digital economy minister and a Huawei vice-president covered network expansion, a national data centre, a sovereign cloud, rural connectivity, AI solutions, digital public services, intelligent monitoring, digital skills and technology centres, and are stated to be heading for a comprehensive memorandum and a framework agreement on priority projects](2026-07-03-guinea-huawei-deepen-strategic-partnership).

No memorandum or framework agreement is signed, and no contract value for any of it is held.

summary: A [European co-financed cable](2026-05-06-mediaguinee-medusa-africa-second-submarine-cable-cma) reached a construction and maintenance agreement in May 2026 for a Mediterranean-anchored system.
developments:
The agreement is the only European engagement the base holds ([agreement](2026-05-06-mediaguinee-medusa-africa-second-submarine-cable-cma)).

No programme, financing envelope or cooperation instrument accompanies it, so European involvement in the country's digital build reaches the record as one cable and nothing else.

progress: No change, nothing on the record since 2019
summary: India's one Guinea-specific digital instrument is the [e-VBAB memorandum with TCIL, signed in Conakry on 2 August 2019](2025-02-14-bilateral-brief-india-guinea-relations).
developments:
[Of three memoranda signed in Conakry on 2 August 2019 during the Indian president's state visit, one is between Guinea's higher education ministry and Telecommunications Consultants India Limited for participation in the e-VBAB Network Project, the technology upgrade of India's Pan-African e-Network tele-education and telemedicine satellite platform](2025-02-14-bilateral-brief-india-guinea-relations).

It is the only Guinea-specific Indian digital instrument on the record, and nothing reports its operation, its outcome or any successor.
